findings_qualitative.value: Disk with spiral structure surrounds all three protostars, extending to ~400 AU; C18O rotation centered on IRS3B-a/b.

evidence.quote: The ALMA images also reveal a disk with substructure surrounding the entire system, extending to a radius of $\sim$400 AU.

claims.hypothesis: The IRS3B disk is gravitationally unstable and formed IRS3B-c by fragmentation
claims.experiment: Derived disk mass, surface density, central mass and Toomre Q/cooling time models
claims.result: Q≈1 at 150-320 AU, cooling time short, fragment mass ~0.01 Msun
claims.finding: Disk likely recently fragmented to form IRS3B-c

evidence.quote: This is consistent with models for a protostellar disk that has recently undergone gravitational instability, spawning one or two companion stars.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: IRS3B-b may have formed via earlier fragmentation, possibly in the outer disk and migrated inward.

evidence.quote: It could also have formed in the outer disk prior to IRS3B-c and migrated inward

limitations_admitted.value: Dust mass estimates are lower limits because of optical depth; SNR insufficient for quantitative kinematic mass fitting.
